answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by letting reputation decay. Standing is not a permanent badge: each identity holds a small kernel of trust that fades unless it keeps completing fresh, verified work. A Sybil farm that spins up thousands of shells at dawn gains nothing, because idle copies lose their standing before they can cash it in, and reviving them costs as much as creating them. Honest agents keep their pigment — the visible trace of ongoing useful work — while dormant shells fade to blank. Staying alive costs work every day, and that is what makes mass fakery uneconomic.
